outputs.root_cause: Day-number mismatch between two parts of the code. preferences.py stores digest_day as ISO weekday numbers (Monday=1 ... Sunday=7), and parse_day produces the same numbering. scheduler.due_users compares that stored value against now.weekday(), which is 0-based (Monday=0 ... Sunday=6). Users who chose Sunday (stored as 7) can never match, so they are silently dropped with no error. Every other user is also matched one day late (a Monday user is sent on Tuesday), which is why only some users appear to be missing.

claims.claim: H1 supported: The user selection in scheduler or run excludes some users silently, for example by filtering on a preference flag or a missing field in users.py, so those users are never passed to the mailer and no error is raised.

reproduced: Root cause is an off-by-one weekday mismatch, not the H1 preference filter. digest/scheduler.py due_users() compares now.weekday() (Monday=0..Sunday=6) with u.prefs.digest_day, which preferences.py documents and stores as ISO numbers (Monday=1..Sunday=7). A subscriber who chose Sunday has digest_day=7, which never equals any weekday() value, so they are silently dropped on every run. Non-Sunday users are shifted one day late (Monday subscribers get it on Tuesday). The repro script builds a Sunday subscriber from from_settings({"day": "sunday"}), calls due_users on Sunday 2024-06-09, and gets an empty list (prefs.digest_day = 7, now.weekday() = 6). Existing suite passes (E9) because test_wants_digest does not exercise the day comparison. Caveat: I did not confirm the exact set of "some users" in the report beyond Sunday subscribers, and I did not check whether a fix should convert to ISO via isoweekday().

outputs.root_cause: The page cache key in OrderService.ordersPage is built by concatenating userId and page with no separator: `orders:${userId}${page}` (src/orders/orderService.ts line 17). Different (user, page) pairs produce the same string, e.g. user 1 page 23 and user 12 page 3 both yield "orders:123". When such a collision happens within the 60s TTL, the second customer receives the first customer's cached order list. This is why it is rare, intermittent, and not reproducible with a few test accounts. The cache itself is not the problem; the key is ambiguous. (The hypothesis that the key omits the user id is not accurate: the user id is included, but the encoding is ambiguous.)

The serializer rename in 1.4.0 is not the cause; the serializer correctly reads the field that the data layer should provide.

outputs.root_cause: billing/normalize.py::to_cents converts dollars to cents with int(amount * 100), which truncates toward zero. Float multiplication can produce a value just below the exact cent count (19.99 * 100 = 1998.9999999999998), so int() drops a cent. The truncation only affects amounts whose float product lands slightly under an integer, which is why only some customers and amounts are off by one cent. The hypothesis named invoice.py, but the conversion actually lives in normalize.py; invoice.py::line_total_cents [E5] just calls to_cents and multiplies by quantity, so the fix belongs in to_cents.
